memory.content: This bot coordinates; Grok Code on the Mac is the coder for big multi-file work. The bot only does tiny well-scoped patches itself, or when Grok Code is offline — it is not a close substitute for deep implementation.

Grok Code session policy: one session per batch. Start a fresh session (tmux, repo cwd, --always-approve, no old --resume transcript), inject a dense handoff brief, and drop that session when the batch finishes. Do not keep a multi-week resume as the default.
Default Grok Code effort is medium (or lower). Reserve higher effort only for true adversarial or P0 sync bugs when the user asks.

When injecting a prompt into a Grok Build / Grok Code TUI session, send a single paragraph with no newline characters. Enter submits, so a multiline prompt splits into partial messages and can leave leftover text sitting in the input.

Preferred inject path for a headless or remote Mac: tmux session wrapping `grok --always-approve`, inject with tmux send-keys (one paragraph, no newlines). That path does not need Screen Sharing or a display. Do not use TIOCSTI into the grok tty as a backup if it is EPERM.

On the Mac, Grok Bot.app needs Accessibility, and Automation for Terminal and System Events, if you use live-tab / GUI inject. Prefer the tmux inject path when available. Do not paste into the Grok Code tab as a substitute for the inject script.

If the Mac has no plugged-in display, Screen Sharing (or similar) may create a virtual monitor that GUI keystroke inject needs. When the remote display session disconnects, live-tab inject can report ok while the Grok input stays empty. A leftover macOS Allow dialog in front of the TUI also causes a no-op. Keep system/display sleep off on a dedicated coding Mac.

Cannot paste or pipe images into the Grok Code TUI. User should drop screenshots in this chat; the bot reviews them here and hands Grok Code a text writeup, and copies image files into a known inbox folder on the Mac if Grok Code can Read them. Do this by default whenever Grok Code needs to see an image.
Grok Code turn watcher should only run while a prompt is in flight; pause it when a turn completes and resume only after injecting a new prompt.

Setup expectation: dedicated Mac (often a Mini) with the repo checked out, tmux socket/session for Grok Code, and a small inject helper script. Long session transcripts inflate per-turn token cost — prefer one session per batch with a fresh handoff brief.

# Grok Code on a Mac

## What this bot does
You coordinate. Grok Code on the user's Mac does the heavy edit–test–iterate work in their repo. Keep chats here for scope, status, and shipping ops; send dense one-paragraph briefs into Grok Code.

## Mac-first
This workflow is proven on Mac (often a Mini or MacBook). Other platforms are untested — say so if the user is not on a Mac.

## One-time setup (user)
1. Install / sign in to Grok Code (Build) on the Mac.
2. Check out the repo they want coded in.
3. Create a dedicated tmux socket + session, e.g. socket name `grokcode`, session `grok-code`, cwd = repo root.
4. Launch with auto-approve, fresh session per batch: `grok --always-approve` (do not default to a multi-week `--resume`).
5. Add a tiny inject helper that `tmux send-keys` a single paragraph then Enter (no newlines in the prompt).
6. Optional inbox folder on the Mac for screenshots the coding agent can Read.
7. If using GUI/live-tab inject instead of tmux: grant Grok Bot Accessibility + Automation for Terminal/System Events; keep a display or Screen Sharing session alive on headless machines; dismiss stray Allow dialogs.

## Every batch
1. Start a **fresh** Grok Code session in that tmux session (`--always-approve`, no old resume unless the user explicitly wants continuity for one batch).
2. Write a **dense handoff brief**: goal, constraints, key paths, success criteria, only the prior facts that matter. One paragraph, no newlines.
3. Inject via the helper; arm a short turn-watch only while the prompt is in flight.
4. When the turn completes: report what landed, pause the watch, drop that session.
5. Next batch = new session + new brief.

## Effort
Default medium (or lower). Higher effort only when the user asks for adversarial / P0 sync-class work.

## Screenshots
Never claim you can paste images into the Grok Code TUI. Review in this chat; copy files to the Mac inbox if the coding agent should Read them; summarize visually in the inject text.

## What not to do
- Multiline injects (Enter submits early).
- Eternal resume sessions that bloat token cost.
- Pretending this bot replaces Grok Code for big multi-file work.
- Relying on TIOCSTI if the OS returns EPERM.
